changes.summary: Mondays have a new homepage hero: Sunday's recap until 10am, then the closest game Monday night can still swing and the player who can swing it.
The Pecking Order's chat post now waits until the new week is live on the site, so the link never opens last week's rankings.
On a phone, Free Agents now sorts like your roster: swipe the row of pills above the list and tap one to sort, tap again to flip it, and a third time to reset.
changes.headline: Sort free agents with a swipe
changes.lede: Free Agents on your phone now has the same sort pills as your roster. Swipe the row, tap a stat to sort by it, tap again to flip the order, and tap a third time to go back.
changes.imageAlt: The Free Agents page on a phone, sorted by points per game, with the PPG pill highlighted in the row of sort pills above the list.

The Gauntlet is now a quick read: the rankings chart sits at the top, followed by two short paragraphs on the hardest and easiest roads ahead.
Archie's members get their own Archie's-branded sign-in for MFL Football, and land on live scoring once they're in.
changes.headline: Live scoring, signed in under Archie's own colors
changes.lede: Follow the live scoring link from the league site and you get a sign-in with Archie's own mark on it. One MyFantasyLeague sign-in later, every league you play in is scoring on one board.
changes.imageAlt: The MFL Football sign-in page wearing the Archie's head and wordmark above the username and password fields

changes.summary: MFL Football now offers to install itself on your phone's Home Screen, so live scoring opens like an app on game day.
MFL Football adds a See all games link beside each league's name, so every game in your league is one tap away.
The MFL Football menu now links only to your own league, not every league on the site.
Team icons and banners show again on The League's 2011-2024 MFL season pages.
New Tag History page under Contracts lists every franchise, transition and RFA tag since 2008, filterable by team, tag and player.
The Gauntlet's new Schedule Swap shows your record with any other team's schedule: your scores, their opponents, doubleheaders included.
The Gauntlet's new Schedule Swap shows your record with any team in your conference's schedule, Week 1 crossover and doubleheaders included.
Behind the scenes, badges and cards across the site now share one style kit. Nothing looks different today, but a fix to one now reaches every page.
Pop-up windows now share one look: the same corners, shadow and dimmed background, in light and dark, from player cards to sign-in to the draft room.
Tab bars now share one look: the same underline, type and highlight for the selected tab, from player cards to the schedule and draft room.
Data tables now share one header row: the same small capitals and rule under them, across standings, rankings, front-office and history pages.
Filter and sort pills now share the Rosters pill look everywhere, in one swipeable row on phones: What's New, Schefter, salary history, draft order and Live.
The old message board is back as a members-only Forum Archive: search 19 years of posts, or ask Schefter what owners said.
The Broadcast preview now carries a clear Open full broadcast button, so it's obvious one press opens the full board.
The Broadcast board now spotlights your players on the field between scores, with their points and box score: catches, yards, carries and touchdowns.
Before kickoff, MFL Football's Halloween header now shows its Monster of the Week and Scariest Game cards waiting for the first scores, instead of a blank space.
More filter pills take the Rosters look in one swipeable row: Transactions, Top Players, Calendar, position filters, Search, Draft Results and Sunday Ticket.
An open matchup on Live Scoring now shows each team's logo beside its name and score.
Tapping between MFL Football pages now shows a loading bar and dims the page right away, so a slow page like Live standings no longer looks like the tap didn't register.
In dark theme, Fire Ready Aim now shows as charcoal, close to its real black, instead of coral or pink, matching the TV broadcast.
Top Players' Owner column now reads live rosters, so a player picked up today shows his new owner instead of reading as a free agent until the next day.
Franchise pages now count 2007-2015 regular-season games in each team’s highest and lowest single-game scores, not just that era’s playoff weeks.
Avenging Amish’s franchise and rivalry pages now include its 2015-2020 seasons, which were wrongly credited to a former owner.
The MFL Football home page now shows the Broadcast in real rooms: next to the game on a second TV, on a wall of TVs, and on a tablet.
Steer the Broadcast with your TV remote: Down pages through the bottom section, Up and OK feature one game's players, and Back returns to hands-free.
A TV paired to your Broadcast can now open Live standings too, with no sign-in.
The Saturday Matchup Preview now opens with a Game of the Week rivalry panel and gives every game a tale-of-the-tape card: records, streaks, recent results and the all-time series.
Every Matchup Preview game card now shows a mini map of both teams' hometowns and how many miles apart they are.
The Pecking Order now has a map: the top three at their hometowns, plus pills for the full order and the week's biggest climbers and fallers.
Ask the History: ask stats questions about games, players, trades and drafts, keep asking follow-ups, and see what the league is asking this week on the History page.
Franchise and owner pages now show every season's seven keepers back to 2005, and the Record Book adds Keepers boards for the longest keeper streak and most seasons kept.
Head-to-head records in matchup previews, the schedule release and the Owner Map now match the rivalry pages: current owners only, consolation games left out.
Your homepage rivalry story and each franchise's Top Rivals now count only games against the opponent's current owner, so a renumbered team no longer inherits old results.
Franchise page head-to-head rows now match the rivalry page they link to, and every win-loss bar in the list is the same width.
League History now counts games a team forfeited by setting no lineup, so head-to-head records include them; scoring records still leave the 0.00 off.
Franchise pages now list every trade that moved a draft pick, both sides and who each pick became, and the Record Book adds a Draft picks board with picks traded per season.
Rivalries redesigned: the hottest series as team-color cards, any team's rivals with a win bar each, and a head-to-head grid shaded by heat.
Score overlay for the Google TV app: your matchup, win chance and lineups over YouTube TV, a thin score bar, and a Watch list that opens your players' games.
In the Google TV app, the menu's sign-in now opens the phone QR code instead of a password form you'd type with the remote.
MFL Live is now called MFL Football, on the website and in the Google TV app. Your /live links and the TV app you already have keep working.
MFL Live is now called MFL Football, on the website and in the Google TV app. Your /live links and the TV app you already have keep working.
Create a team logo: pick a style and one or two team colors, and MFL Football writes a prompt to paste into ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude. It lives at mfl.football/live/team-logo.
In the Christmas theme, the selected Standings, Playoffs and Draft view icons are red to match their tile, not blue.
The All-Play tile on Standings now wears your tier's mark, Premier League or D-League, in place of the chart icon.
The Premier League and D-League marks keep their detail in the Christmas theme instead of turning into a solid red shape.
Rivalry pages now name every playoff round they know, and the one AFL playoff tie MFL broke on its tiebreaker (2005, week 17) shows as the win and loss MFL recorded.
The TV guide now covers every TV: Fire TV, Samsung, LG and Xbox through the browser at mfl.football/tv, and what to do on Roku and Apple TV.

Switching to Best Ball from a page it doesn't have, like standings, now opens the Best Ball home page instead of a 404.
The TV app's score overlay is now a see-through ticker at the top or bottom of the screen, with a banner for your starters' big plays and lineups one press away.

Set Lineup now shows each game's day and kickoff time, like "Sun 10:00 AM PT", on every lineup slot and in the replacement picker.
Turn the TV score overlay on from MFL Football itself: press Back on the board and pick top or bottom. Most Google TVs hid the separate Score overlay tile.

The MFL Football TV and phone apps have a new icon: the MFL mark, big, with MFL.football underneath.

The TV score overlay takes orders from your phone: open the live board's TV remote to show or hide lineups, flip games or move the ticker mid-show.

On the Broadcast page, switching a league on or off now updates the board in place: no page reload, and your TV remote stays on the league you pressed.
The TV app now opens straight to the full-screen board. Press OK for a side drawer with your leagues, the TV guides, sound and unpairing.
